proof_summary: For an odd prime, set \(T=2(p-1)\): Fermat’s theorem makes the product factors and triangular-power coefficients invariant under a shift by \(T\), while each extra term with index below \(T\) vanishes because its product contains \(2^T-1\). For \(p=2\), every positive-index summand vanishes and the remaining summand is \(1\), so the result follows separately.
